artists.biography: Jesus Jones are a British alternative dance band. The Wiltshire-based group, formed in late 1988, recorded and performed in the late 1980s, throughout the 1990s, and into the 2000s. They are best remembered for their track, "Right Here, Right Now", an international hit and subsequently globally appropriated for promotional and advertising campaigns. They are also well-remembered for the songs "Real Real Real" and "International Bright Young Thing."

perplexity.description:
Passages, released in 2018 on Demon Records, marks a significant return for Jesus Jones after a lengthy hiatus. Musically, the album blends the band's signature alternative rock foundation with contemporary electronic textures, reflecting both their roots and an openness to modern sonic experimentation. The songwriting is direct and visceral, shaped by the realities of performing in smaller venues and the band's desire to remain immediate and engaging. Themes of life's changes, mortality, and personal reflection run throughout, making Passages one of the most introspective works in their catalog.

In the context of Jesus Jones' discography, Passages stands as their first full-length studio album since 2001's London, and it is widely regarded as their most personal record since 1993's Perverse. The album was preceded by singles "How's This Even Going Down" and "Suck It Up," and it was met with positive critical reception for its energy, honesty, and ability to balance nostalgia with fresh ideas. Reviewers noted that while the album retains the spirit of their earlier work, it also pushes the band into new territory, reaffirming their relevance in the modern rock and electronic landscape.
